rationale: Ratification of LVL0 Revision 1.0.

Editorial amendment, revision 1.0.1: remove a capitalized normative word from the LEX.index definition (a Lexicon definition imposes no obligation); meaning unchanged. Lower governance affected: none.

Editorial amendment, revision 1.0.2: define the roles Author, Adopter, and Auditor, which provisions already use (REPRO.5, QA.7, GOV.34; GOV.41, GOV.42, GOV.46, GOV.49; QA.2, GOV.47); meaning of existing provisions unchanged. Lower governance affected: none.
Editorial amendment, revision 1.0.3: the ratification record names the role that ratified the constitution, The Custodian, in place of a blank; no obligation changes. Lower governance affected: none.

Minor amendment, revision 1.1: Normative Language adds SHOULD NOT (lowercase should not) to the capitalized words and to the table, so that every normative word is fixed in one place; DSGN.13 already used SHOULD NOT with this meaning. Lower governance affected: STND.DRAFT, whose modal table now cites the entry.

Minor amendment, revision 1.2: LVL0 conforms to the drafting standard STND.DRAFT. Forty-two edits across forty provisions replace excluded expressions (prohibited, permitted, ought to, need not, has to, required) with table words, replace the review-class words could and considered, and replace the quantifier any where a plainer word is available. GUARD.18 now names the human owner as the party who records what is practical; no other obligation changes.

Editorial amendment, revision 1.2.1: four phrasings introduced in revision 1.2 (GOV.13, GUARD.12, PRIME.13, QA.3) used at will, which the drafting standard reads as SHALL; they now read throughout the project's life or whenever the actor chooses. No obligation changes.

Review of STND.DRAFT revision 0.3 under QA.7 by the custodian, an actor other than its author. The review covers the change the reviewer instructed, the SHOULD NOT row of the modal table, and accepts that provisions 3, 14, and 23 are checked by the reader and that review-class flags remain for the reader to judge. The scope pins the exact content reviewed; any later edit to STND/DRAFT is a change outside the ledger until reviewed again.

Adoption of STND.DRAFT, revision 1.0, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-09 after the QA.7 review of revision 0.3 (ledger entry 8). Revision 1.0 changes only the status, revision, adoption date, and revision history of revision 0.3; no provision changes.

Adoption of STND.IDENT, revision 1.0, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-09. Revision 1.0 carries the twelve provisions of revision 0.3, which was presented for review on the same day; adoption changes only the status, revision, adoption date, and revision history. It covers revision numbers only; the identifier syntax and the mnemonic register follow as a minor amendment.

Editorial amendment of STND.DRAFT, revision 1.0.1, approved by the custodian on 2026-10-09. The adoption of revision 1.0 (ledger entry 9) set the status of the standard but left its 33 provisions at draft; each now carries the status adopted and the adoption date. Class: editorial, because no obligation, permission, or defined meaning changes (STND.IDENT.3).

Review of STND.IDENT revision 0.3 under QA.7 by the custodian, an actor other than its author. The custodian states that the review was implicit in the ratification of 2026-10-09 (ledger entry 10) and is recorded here after it. Revision 1.0 carries the reviewed provision text unchanged; the scope pins that content.
Review of STND.CLASS revision 0.4 under QA.7 by the custodian, an actor other than its author, recorded at the custodian's statement on 2026-10-09. The scope pins the content reviewed.

Adoption of STND.CLASS, revision 1.0, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-09 after the QA.7 review of revision 0.4 (ledger entry 13). Adoption changes only the status, revision, adoption dates, and revision history; no provision text changes.

Ruling of the custodian under GOV.3, 2026-10-09: the adopter's recorded decision to adopt or amend a governance document satisfies the QA.7 review of that revision. No retrospective review transactions are needed for LVL0 revisions 1.0.1 to 1.2.1 or STND.DRAFT revision 1.0.1. STND.IDENT revision 1.1 records this rule as a provision.

Minor amendment of STND.CLASS, revision 1.1, approved by the custodian on 2026-10-09 from the global consistency review (items A1 to A6). The reliance tests of STND.CLASS.1 follow GOV.12 again: a system that acts unattended places work in CSQ1, and CSQ3 reliance is limited to the author or actors of the same unit of work. STND.CLASS.18 drops its CSQ4 row. New STND.CLASS.20 makes the proportionality judgment for a result the classification's entry and requires a promotion to cite it. STND.CLASS.7 says reassess; STND.CLASS.10 uses the Lexicon's reference oracle; the Terms drop Reviewer and Independent reference; two informative sentences are corrected. Class: minor, because obligations change while the motivation of the standard does not. Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Minor amendment, revision 1.3, approved by the custodian on 2026-10-09 from the global consistency review (items B1 to B6). The Lexicon adds the roles Reviewer (QA.7, QA.8) and Standards owner (GOV.41, PRIME.1); Promotion makes a result reportable at the level of obligations its proportionality judgment sets, where it had misused evidence level; Amendment covers every adopted governance document; Auditor covers compliance audits (GOV.47); Normative Language lists NEVER in place of SHALL NEVER; two governed_by fields name sections as locators. Class: minor, because defined meanings change while no obligation or principle does. Lower governance affected: STND.CLASS (Reviewer, already removed from its Terms by revision 1.1), STND.DRAFT.29 (the role word reviewer is now defined). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Minor amendment of STND.IDENT, revision 1.1, approved by the custodian on 2026-10-09 from the global consistency review (items C1 and C2) and the ruling of ledger entry 15 (item D). New STND.IDENT.13 requires the QA.7 review of each revision to be recorded no later than its transaction and lets the adopter's recorded decision serve as that review. STND.IDENT.6 fixes how amendments are cited in a revision history (GOV.40 for LVL0, GOV.41 otherwise). STND.IDENT.3 and STND.IDENT.4 also instantiate GOV.41; STND.IDENT.9 instantiates GOV.43 in place of GOV.37. Class: minor, because obligations are added while the scheme of revision numbers does not change. Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Annotation of ledger entries 1 to 18, whose actor field is blank. The actor of every one of them is The Custodian, who decided each transaction. The text of every revision and ruling they record from entry 2 onward was authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), in a Cowork session at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5); entry 1 records the ratification of text likewise drafted with that agent. From entry 19 the actor field is filled and agent authorship is stated in each rationale.

Editorial amendment of STND.DRAFT, revision 1.0.2, approved by the custodian on 2026-10-10: the table of STND.DRAFT.29 drops the row that listed reviewer as an undefined role word, since LVL0 revision 1.3 (ledger entry 17) defines Reviewer in the Lexicon. Class: editorial, because check g.19 already treats a Lexicon role as defined and no obligation changes. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Editorial amendment of STND.CLASS, revision 1.1.1, approved by the custodian on 2026-10-10: the CSQ3 row of STND.CLASS.19 names the auditor as an actor who is not an author of the audited work, the wording of the other rows, in place of an actor other than the author. Class: editorial, because the audited work's author is the same actor either way. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Minor amendment of STND.CLASS, revision 1.2, approved by the custodian on 2026-10-10: the term Credible consequence covers a chain of events in a foreseeable misuse of the work as well as in its intended use. Before, the term narrowed the worst credible consequence of GOV.12 to the intended use, which PRIME.15 forbids. Class: minor, because a defined meaning changes while the motivation of the standard does not. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Minor amendment, revision 1.4, approved by the custodian on 2026-10-10: the Lexicon defines Review as the examination of a change before release (QA.7), yet LVL0 also applies the word to a threat model (GUARD.16), an axiom (VV.9), pinned revisions (REPRO.9), knowledge entries (GOV.34), lower provisions (GOV.42), standards at an interval (GOV.46), and a conflict referred for ruling (GOV.4). The entry now states that, applied to anything other than a change, the word carries its ordinary meaning of a re-examination. Class: minor, because a defined meaning changes while no obligation does. Lower governance affected: none. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Editorial amendment of STND.CLASS, revision 1.2.1, approved by the custodian on 2026-10-10: the front-matter field withdrawn lists STND.CLASS.8, STND.CLASS.9, and STND.CLASS.11 to STND.CLASS.16, which revision 0.2 withdrew and the informative text already names, so that the harness is able to keep them from reuse (GOV.37). Class: editorial, because it records a fact already stated and changes no obligation. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Minor amendment of STND.IDENT, revision 1.2, approved by the custodian on 2026-10-10: new STND.IDENT.14 requires a document to list in its front-matter field withdrawn the identifier of each provision a revision withdraws, and forbids giving a withdrawn identifier to another provision (GOV.37). New check v.8 fails on a gap in a document's numbering that the field does not list, on a listed identifier that is in use, and on a listed identifier of another document. Before, the withdrawn identifiers of STND.CLASS were protected only by prose. Class: minor, because an obligation is added while the scheme of revision numbers does not change. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Editorial amendment of STND.DRAFT, revision 1.0.3, approved by the custodian on 2026-10-10: the table of STND.DRAFT.29 is tidied. The eleven undefined role words follow the two retired words in alphabetical order, and their Replace with entry reads a defined role in place of eleven repetitions of a role the Lexicon or the Terms section defines, which the provision's first sentence states once. Class: editorial, because no word changes class and no obligation changes. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Minor amendment of STND.IDENT, revision 1.3, approved by the custodian on 2026-10-10: the section Identifiers gains STND.IDENT.15 to STND.IDENT.23, which fix the forms of identifiers, locators, slugs, and mnemonics, the choice of mnemonics, the mnemonic register MNEM that GOV.37 requires, its register transactions and permanent rows, the use of mnemonics and grades, and the custodians' authority to register mnemonics (GOV.41). Terms gains Number, Grade, Parent, Letter distance, and Retired item. New checks v.9 to v.11 enforce the forms, the register, and its transactions. Class: minor, because obligations are added while the scheme of revision numbers does not change. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Initial content of the mnemonic register MNEM (STND.IDENT.19, STND.IDENT.20), approved by the custodian on 2026-10-10: 57 active rows, giving every mnemonic in use under its parent, the grades of the scales LVL, CSQ, and EVD, and the mnemonics of the kinds of LVL3 instrument under the parent project. The STND second-level mnemonics, until now proposals, become final. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Minor amendment of STND.DRAFT, revision 1.1, approved by the custodian on 2026-10-10: the term Locator defers to STND.IDENT.15 for the form of a locator and to STND.IDENT.16 for its slug, which replaces each run of characters other than the letters a to z and the digits 0 to 9 with one hyphen, where the former term joined words with hyphens. Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Minor amendment, revision 1.5, approved by the custodian on 2026-10-10: GUARD.7 adds the removal or overwriting of temporary items to the grounds on which the reserved-action register exempts a class from GUARD.5, so that routine cleanup of intermediates marked as temporary from their creation is not reserved. The Lexicon defines Temporary item (an item created to hold an intermediate, recorded as temporary from its creation, that no record cites) and amends Irrecoverable action to exclude an action of an exempt class, which closes a gap by which PRIME.6 still reserved an exempt action. GUARD.6 still prevails over every exemption, so an unlisted mass deletion stays reserved. Alternatives weighed: confining the exemption to regenerable content, which leaves non-regenerable scratch output reserved; exempting stale items, rejected because nothing records that nothing relies on them; and a numeric bulk size, rejected by the custodian. Class: minor, because obligations change while no prime directive or principle changes in motivation or intent. Lower governance affected: STND.DFLT, whose draft uses the new ground; no adopted standard. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Annotation of ledger entry 30. Entry 30 records the custodian's ratification of LVL0 revision 1.5, given on 2026-10-10 before it was appended, and its rationale is the ratified proposal. An agent error appended it before the amended text reached the corpus: a rehearsal script ran the live ledger tool, so entry 30 pins the content of revision 1.4. This entry pins the content of revision 1.5 as ratified, which differs from revision 1.4 only by the change entry 30 describes. Entry 30 is not edited (PRIME.5). Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Register change, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-10: MNEM gains the mnemonic SIGNR for the signer register, whose keys the harness uses to verify signatures on ledger entries (GOV.36, STND.DFLT.23); the custodians found the register later, with the anchor key of the human owner. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Adoption of STND.DFLT, revision 1.0, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-10 after review of draft 0.3: 26 binding provisions that provide the mechanisms of GOV.21 and the ledger of GOV.36 for work without a project constitution (GOV.22), including a signed work ledger, listed scope for destructive actions and remote writes, bounds of reach, and no time limits. Adopted after LVL0 1.5 (GUARD.7) and the MNEM row SIGNR, on which STND.DFLT.15 and STND.DFLT.23 rest, and before the re-derived STND.INSTR, which STND.DFLT.21 takes in once adopted. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Minor amendment of STND.DRAFT, revision 1.2, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-10: new STND.DRAFT.34 requires each document below LVL0 to hold, before its revision history, a section References whose table gives the identifier and title of each document it cites, because the number of mnemonics and cross-references has grown. The Terms define Cited document. The table is derived from the corpus by the harness and checked by g.25. Alternatives weighed: covering LVL0, rejected because LVL0 cites only its own parts; one row per top-level mnemonic, rejected because STND.CLASS and STND.IDENT would collapse into one row. Class: minor, because an obligation is added. Lower governance affected: STND.IDENT, STND.CLASS, and STND.DFLT, which conform by editorial amendments that follow; drafts conform on re-derivation. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Adoption of STND.INSTR, revision 1.0, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-10 after review of draft 0.2: eight binding provisions of agent practice that LVL0 and STND.DFLT state only as outcomes (recoverable prior state, protected locations, dry runs, failure stops, injected instructions, completion reports, and session notes), which STND.DFLT.21 makes the agent instructions of work without a project constitution. The undivided draft 0.1 is archived; its restatements of LVL0 and its default standing authorization are dropped (GOV.22). Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Editorial amendment of STND.DFLT, revision 1.0.2, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-10: the informative notes drop the clause that STND.DFLT.21 supplies no agent instructions until STND.INSTR is adopted, which its adoption (ledger entry 38) made stale. Class: editorial, because the notes are informative and no obligation changes. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Minor amendment of STND.DFLT, revision 1.1, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-10: STND.DFLT.15 gains a fifth exempt class, a change or removal of an item that a checkpoint covers, where an entry that STND.DFLT.23 accepts records the mechanism that takes the checkpoint and the actions it covers (GUARD.7: the prior state is verifiably recoverable). The class names no method: an editing tool's checkpoints, a hook that snapshots before each command, or a file-system snapshot each qualify for the actions the record names, and the agent relies on the human owner's signed record, not its own judgment (GUARD.2). It removes the need to commit before each covered change (STND.INSTR.2). Alternatives weighed: naming a tool or method, rejected because environments differ (GOV.18); counting checkpoints without a record, rejected under GUARD.2; widening the snapshot class, rejected because a checkpoint is not verified per action; no exemption, rejected as needless friction. Class: minor, because an exemption is added. Lower governance affected: STND.INSTR.2 defers to STND.DFLT.15 and needs no change. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Minor amendment of STND.INSTR, revision 1.1, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-10: STND.INSTR.2 requires the prior state to be preserved outside the action's scope rather than committed, stashed, or copied; STND.INSTR.4 applies to any means of a destructive action that offers a dry run, not only a command; STND.INSTR.5 requires a procedure of more than one step to halt on a failed step or an unresolved input rather than naming shell variables; the term Dry run and the protected location of the primary copy of the work drop tool vocabulary; the notes state that environment means are derived from the standard and recorded under STND.DFLT.22. Class: minor, because the wording of obligations changes, though their outcome does not. Alternatives weighed: keeping tool names as examples in the provisions, rejected under STND.DRAFT.12 and GOV.18. Lower governance affected: none adopted. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Minor amendment of STND.DFLT, revision 1.2, ratified by the custodian: signatures and fail-closed configuration are kept for assured work, recorded as CSQ0 or CSQ1, where a forged authorization or an unenforced outcome risks major or irreversible harm, and made optional elsewhere, as the custodian directed, because friction at every class invites circumvention. For assured work, an entry counts only with the human owner's signature confirmed by a verifier the agent is unable to alter, and a configuration displaces a provision only while such a verifier finds it installed. For other work, an unsigned entry of the human owner, or an agent's record of a grant (STND.DFLT.17), carries an authorization across sessions, and a configuration, which may then fail open, displaces nothing. A checkpoint mechanism exempts a change only while found installed in the session. Every provision thus applies when a harness or configuration is lost. The floor (GOV.10) holds: each class's mechanism meets GUARD and GOV, and STND.DFLT.5 and PRIME.7 still bar a forged entry, which for other work nothing detects. No class is assumed (GOV.13): an unsigned entry makes work assured, and only a signed one ends that. Class: minor (STND.IDENT.3), because obligations change and no prime directive or principle does. Alternatives weighed: signatures at every class, rejected by the custodian; none at any class, rejected for CSQ0 and CSQ1; a configuration that displaces provisions while nothing shows it failing, rejected because a lost configuration shows nothing. Lower governance affected: none adopted; STND.INSTR.2 defers to STND.DFLT.15. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Adoption of STND.HARN, revision 1.0, ratified by the custodian after review of draft 0.7: 25 binding provisions on read-only retrieval, the form of the corpus and the ledgers, signatures, generated content, checks, the optional derivation of an agent's environment, and rehearsal. A harness serves governance read-only and no work depends on it (GOV.38). Drafts 0.1 to 0.6 were reviewed independently in harness reviews 0002 to 0007. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Editorial amendment of STND.DRAFT, revision 1.2.1, directed by the custodian: the informative Checks section names `python -m govharness` commands instead of the scripts that STND.HARN 1.0 retires; no obligation changes. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Editorial amendment of STND.IDENT, revision 1.3.2, directed by the custodian: the informative Checks section names `python -m govharness` commands instead of the scripts that STND.HARN 1.0 retires; no obligation changes. Minor amendment, revision 1.6, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-11: GOV.18 reserves to LVL3 any limit, beyond those of LVL0, on the number of agents an agent directs, the depth of delegation, and network access made to retrieve information for research, so that no profile or standard caps agent teams or research retrieval across projects. Alternatives weighed: a provision of the AGENT profile barring LVL2 limits (rejected: it would narrow GOV.18 against PRIME.15), a custodians' decision (rejected: it does not bind later standards), and a note only (rejected: binds nothing). Lower governance affected: AGENT; STND.DFLT sets no such limit; STND.PROJ to carry fields for project limits. Proposal: claude/downstream/adopted-instruments-2026-10-11.md, section 1. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Interpretation of the custodian under GOV.3, adopted 2026-10-11: for GOV.32, a project's workbench is a record of that project's work and not a knowledge base; the knowledge base to which the AGENT profile proposes entries is one shared across projects and managed apart from any one of them; the working-notes workspace and temporary items are neither. A tool is not itself a knowledge entry; an entry concerning a tool is a claim about it, as the Lexicon defines a knowledge entry. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5).

Interpretation of the custodian under GOV.3, adopted 2026-10-11: for PRIME.10, a secret is information whose disclosure would present a security or privacy risk to a person or an organization, above all information that would ease the introduction or exploitation of a vulnerability, such as a password, a key, a token, or a non-public host name, address, account, network layout, open service, or configuration. An identity of hardware or software recorded under REPRO.1, REPRO.2, or REPRO.9 is not a secret where the record is read only by those whom the threat model trusts with it (GUARD.16), and elsewhere is a secret only where its disclosure would ease the introduction or exploitation of a vulnerability. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5).

Adoption of the LVL1 profile AGENT, revision 1.0, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-11 after review of candidate 0.9 by two independent agent reviewers: 46 provisions of agent practice that bind every project (AGENT.1), on explanations and evidence, effort and delegation, autonomy and continuity, scope, observability, recordkeeping, knowledge, the workbench, parallel work, research retrieval, and secret handling. Transition period (GOV.28, GOV.42): none; the profile takes effect on ratification. One editorial correction before entry: AGENT.45 reads 'refer to the human owner its need for that credential' so that the drafting check g.5 does not read 'the need to' as an excluded expression; no obligation changes. Drafts 0.1 to 0.9 and the ratification package are in claude/drafts/. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Minor amendment of STND.DFLT, revision 1.3, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-11: new STND.DFLT.27 fixes the access descriptors of network access records (AGENT.23) as one kind (search, retrieve, write) and one outcome (ok, refused, failed) joined by a colon, a closed list of nine descriptors from six words; the Purpose, the Mechanisms table, the Notes, and References conform. Proposal: claude/drafts/dflt-1.3-descriptors-proposal.md. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Editorial amendment of STND.INSTR, revision 1.1.1, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-11: the notes state that effort estimation and delegation sizing are in the adopted AGENT profile (AGENT.6 to AGENT.10), in place of a clause that its adoption made stale, and References lists AGENT; no obligation changes. Text authored by an agent, Claude (Anthropic), at the custodian's direction (REPRO.5). Under the ruling of ledger entry 15, this decision is the QA.7 review.

Minor amendment of STND.DRAFT, revision 1.3, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-11. Class: minor, because obligations are added. New binding provisions STND.DRAFT.35 to STND.DRAFT.41 fix how selected profiles combine: selector attributes and sub-profile coverage, domain-item and execution-path subjects, shared matters with one owning profile, boundary obligations, and evidence by content; eight terms are defined. New binding STND.DRAFT.42 bars profiles and LVL2 standards from requiring a decision of the human owner that LVL0 neither requires nor reserves, has them accept standing authorizations wherever LVL0 permits, and limits each referral's halt to the line of work it concerns. STND.DRAFT.42 makes STND.DFLT.12, the default working bounds of STND.DFLT, and the remote-write row of STND.HARN.18 nonconforming; they conform by the amendments entered next (ledger entries 53 and 56), and STND.INSTR.6 and STND.HARN.23 are changed with them so that fewer reports reach the human owner (ledger entries 53 and 57); until then work conforming to them is not in defect (GOV.42). The Purpose extends the standard beyond the functions the Lexicon gives a drafting standard to how profiles combine, resting on GOV.11, GOV.24 to GOV.27, and GOV.31. Minor amendment of STND.CODE, revision 1.3, ratified by the custodian on 2026-10-27: new STND.CODE.22 to STND.CODE.26 (defaults; DSGN.4, DSGN.5, and DSGN.14) state for every language the rules on foreign interfaces that STND.CXX, STND.STDC, STND.PY, STND.JL, and STND.RUST held each for its own: the types and the layouts that cross an interface (STND.CODE.22) and its arrays (STND.CODE.23); a failure raised in code that the interface invokes, caught there unless the contract carries it on, and converted to an error of the interface or stored and answered after the call (STND.CODE.24); one owner for each owned resource that crosses, and an object of the work that owns each owned resource that the interface creates for it (STND.CODE.25); and a stated lifetime for each object that foreign code keeps (STND.CODE.26); Terms define Foreign interface once, with what its contract includes, and Owned resource, from STND.CXX; the Purpose lists the new provisions; the Notes give their reasons, their reach in each language, and their onsets. The change is minor under STND.IDENT.3 because it adds five default provisions and two defined meanings. The custodian decided that the shared rules move here, that the language standards keep only what their languages add, and that the rules reach every language (decisions 1 and 4). Against the provisions that they replace, the new ones ask these things more: the alignment of each type and of each compared layout in Python and Julia; the origin of indexes of an array in Python and Julia; the alignment, the compared layouts of a structure, and the element type and the strides of an array, of one dimension or more, in C; the arrays of STND.CODE.23, with their element type and strides, in C++ and Rust; the pass of a foreign resource to its owner before each other operation that is able to fail in Python and Julia; the lifetime of an object that foreign code keeps in C++, C, and Rust; the layout rules in C++; and each of the five in Fortran, Lean, and hardware descriptions, where those have a foreign interface.
